name: Chrome Day — Augmentation Pride Street Festival
creator: Ironbloom Movement / Chrome Children Community Council
description: An annual two-day street festival across Shelf and Tier 2 neighborhoods celebrating augmentation as identity, community, and survival — not aspiration. Chrome Day began as a small Shelf block party and grew into a corridor-spanning event where aug-wearers of every modification level display, discuss, and celebrate their chrome as cultural heritage rather than corporate product. Events include aug-sharing workshops, modification swap meets, live performance, and the Parade of Particular Machines — a procession of the most creatively modified bodies in Meridian.
medium: physical, street festival, pirate neural feed coverage, BCI-shared sensory broadcast
cultural_impact: Chrome Day has shifted the cultural framing of working-class augmentation from 'cheap chrome' shame to visible pride, and its aesthetic vocabulary has influenced Tier 3-4 augmentation fashion in ways that are rarely credited.
controversy: Flatskin and Clearskin anti-augmentation groups protest Chrome Day annually; corporate augmentation brands have repeatedly attempted to co-sponsor the event, each time rejected by the organizing council amid accusations of identity commodification.
story_hooks: A Tier 4 augmentation brand launches a 'Chrome Day Collection' timed to the festival without permission, and the organizing council has to decide between a lawsuit they can't afford and direct action they might regret.
A young Flatskin protester attending Chrome Day to demonstrate is severely injured when a crowd barrier fails — and the Ironbloom medics are the first to reach her.
An elder aug-wearer in the Parade of Particular Machines is carrying illegal military-grade chrome that he's hidden in plain sight for twenty years, and someone in the crowd has just recognized it.
